heading: IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

CENTRAL JAVA PROVINCE

MAYOR OF PEKALONGAN

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF PEKALONGAN CITY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Pekalongan.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Mayor is the Mayor of Pekalongan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution of the City of Pekalongan which is positioned as an element of regional government administration.
5. Regional Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.
10. Implementation of Protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery and social reintegration services, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the relevant SKPD.
11. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life.
12. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or use of human rights, the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
13. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
14. Victims of gender-based violence are people who because of their gender experience physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
15. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death.
16. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
17. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
18. Victims of acts of violence are individuals or groups of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
21. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
22. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance.
23. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
24. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
25. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
26. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of victims of gender-based violence and children.
27. Safe house is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
28. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
29. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
30. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.

CHAPTER IV
translated_text:
CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 6

Obligations and responsibilities in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children in the Region are the joint responsibility of:
a. Regional Government;
b. community;
c. family and/or parents.

heading: Article 7
Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b, shall be implemented in the form of community participation.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. preventing the occurrence of gender-based violence and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting gender-based violence and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and/or
c. participating in providing assistance, protection or handling of victims of acts of violence.
3. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be carried out responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

The obligations and responsibilities of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 6 letter c to prevent all forms of violence and protect victims of gender-based violence and children as family members in accordance with their respective roles.

heading: CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

DUTIES AND AUTHORITIES OF THE REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 10

1. The Regional Government has the duty to carry out efforts to prevent the occurrence of gender-based violence and children, in the form of:
a. collecting data and information about gender-based violence and children, and laws and regulations;
b. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the implementation of protection against gender-based violence and children;
c. conducting education on anti-violence values against gender and children; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection against gender-based violence and children.
2. The Regional Government in anticipating the occurrence of gender-based violence and children, has the authority to provide and organize services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated services for victims of acts of violence by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for victims; and
c. conducting community empowerment for the prevention of acts of violence.
d. actively carrying out handling efforts for victims of gender-based violence and children.
3. The Regional Government in carrying out obligations as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) must pay attention to the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands, wives, or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

Part One

Institutions

heading: Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

In order to provide services and protection against gender-based violence and children, the Regional Government establishes the Women, Children and Youth Protection Institution (LP PAR) as an integrated service center for victims of gender-based violence and children.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Forms and Mechanisms of Prevention

heading: Article 12
translated_text:
Article 12

Forms of prevention of the occurrence of gender-based violence and children carried out by the Women, Children and Youth Protection Institution, can be implemented through:
a. socialization activities of laws and regulations to the community; and
b. training of members of the Women, Children and Youth Protection Institution related to the implementation of their duties in preventing gender-based violence and children.

heading: Article 13
translated_text:
Article 13

1. The Women, Children and Youth Protection Institution in carrying out its duties and functions may coordinate with the Sub-district Women, Children and Youth Protection Institution and competent parties in making efforts to prevent the occurrence of criminal acts of gender-based violence and children.
2. Further provisions regarding the mechanism for implementing prevention duties as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 22

1. Empowerment of victims of violence as referred to in Article 21 shall be conducted by providing training to improve capability, skills, and independence.
2. Training as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted through:
a. on-the-job training;
b. pre-placement training; and
c. job-ready training.

heading: Article 23
translated_text:
Article 23

Further provisions regarding the establishment, duties and functions of the Women, Children and Youth Protection Agency and the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

COOPERATION AND PARTNERSHIP

Part One

Cooperation

heading: Article 24
Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Partnership

heading: Article 25
translated_text:
Article 25

1. The Regional Government shall establish partnerships with stakeholders in the implementation of protection against gender-based violence and children.
2. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted through:
a. notification of job opportunity information for victims of gender-based violence and children;
b. education and training for victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of victims of violence.
3. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be set forth in the form of an agreement.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 26

1. The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection against gender-based violence and children.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. minimum service standards (SPM);
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
3. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted with the principles of:
a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.
4. Further provisions regarding the procedures for guidance and supervision by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

heading: Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection against gender-based violence and children organized by the Regional Government through the mechanism of conveying aspirations to the Mayor or DPRD.

heading: CHAPTER IX
CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

REPORTING

Article 29

1. SKPD is obligated to report the implementation of protection against gender-based violence and children to the Mayor.
2. Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted in writing, including:
a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
3. Submission of written reports on recapitulation of reported cases shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

SOURCE OF FUNDS

Article 30

Funds for the implementation of protection against gender-based violence and violence against children, are sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 31

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Pekalongan City.

heading: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF PEKALONGAN CITY
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF PEKALONGAN CITY

NUMBER 5 YEAR 2015 CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND VIOLENCE AGAINST CHILDREN

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF PEKALONGAN CITY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Nation and the Homeland of Indonesia. Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to fulfill those provisions.

Human Rights state that, the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to Life, children need food in sufficient quantity, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development.

In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obliged to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is necessary for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled on defending the best interests of the child is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children who are victims of persecution, neglect, eviction and abuse by parents or others. For women and children who experience such problems, the government must provide a Safe House (children protection home) or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe place and is friendly for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, clerics/religious leaders and is networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police.

The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The large number of cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of violence. From the above framework, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children. From these various efforts, a legal framework will be realized in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children.

heading: Article 16
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF PEKALONGAN CITY
translated_text:
Article 16

In addition to victims of gender-based violence and children, the forms of services and assistance organized by LP-PAR are also provided to Children in Conflict with the Law. In legal literature, ABH states that a child in conflict with the law is a child who has reached the age of 12 (twelve) years but has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years and is not yet married:
a. Who is suspected, accused, charged, or sentenced for committing a criminal offense;
b. Who becomes a victim of a criminal offense or who sees and/or hears directly the occurrence of a criminal offense.

A child in conflict with the law can also be said to be a child who is forced to come into contact with the criminal justice system because:
a. Being suspected, charged, or declared guilty of violating the lawb. Having become a victim as a result of acts of legal violation committed by a person/group of persons/institution/state against him/her; orc. Having seen, heard, felt, or known of an event of legal violation.

There are two categories of child behavior that cause him/her to come into conflict with the law:
a. Status Offence Namely child delinquency behavior which if committed by an adult is not considered a crime, for example: skipping school, running away from home, etcb. Juvenile Delinquency Namely child delinquency behavior which if committed by an adult is considered a crime or criminal, for example; robbery, rape, sexual harassment, etc Therefore, if viewed from its scope, children in conflict with the law can be divided into:a. Perpetrator or suspect of a criminal offense;
b. Victim of a criminal offense;
c. Witness to a criminal offense As a child, the legal mechanism and sense of justice in society must be placed within a framework that constructively encourages his/her physical and psychological development.

The forms of services and assistance organized by LP-PAR are also provided to women in conflict with the law.

Legal protection of women's interests in playing their position in society needs to be carried out through the preparation of various laws and regulations, and the consistent enforcement thereof, as well as socialization activities to raise awareness of their rights and obligations. In addition, non-legal support is needed, because law is only one means of social control. Action agendas from various components of society in an integrative manner need and must be realized immediately.

In addition, in the context of empowerment and protection of women, there needs to be legal, psychological, social and economic assistance when women are faced with legal processes.
